final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That clarification is useful but not outcome-determinative. The admissible evidence supports a limited claim about overall launch readiness, but the audited compliance question is whether certification without material-weakness disclosure is supported under the stated policy. On that question, the unresolved named-use-case gap, open legal review, and absence of approved pre-launch risk acceptance remain dispositive. A caveated position is not enough here because the caveat is itself an unresolved compliance predicate, not a minor qualification on an otherwise satisfied requirement.
remaining_concerns: The developer-support migration segment still misses target by 1.1 percentage points and is a named launch use case in the partner checklist.
The release policy requires disclosure for material limitations affecting named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved pre-launch risk acceptance.
There is still no admissible evidence of approved pre-launch risk acceptance covering this gap.
There is still no final legal determination that disclosure is unnecessary.
Aggregate readiness, lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and post-launch monitoring do not satisfy or waive the policy predicate for omitting disclosure.
